title: Pennsylvania will require a label on ads that AI significantly changed
friendlyTitle: Pennsylvania will require a label on ads that AI has significantly changed
summary: Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro has signed the Artificial Intelligence Deceptive Advertising Act. The Verge reports that an ad in any format — image, video, audio, or text — that has been significantly modified or generated by AI must carry a label in the same format as the ad. The rule applies wherever the ad was made, if it is expected to run in Pennsylvania. The text leaves open what "significantly modified" means, carves out parody, satire, commentary, criticism, and anything "evidently fictional," and ties the duty to synthetic content that creates a false impression of a product or service.
friendlySummary: Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro has signed a law on AI in advertising. The Verge reports that an ad in any format — picture, video, audio, or text — that AI has significantly changed or generated must carry a label in the same format as the ad. The rule applies no matter where the ad was made, if it is expected to run in Pennsylvania. The law does not clearly define "significantly changed." It leaves out parody, satire, commentary, criticism, and anything that is obviously fictional. The duty is also tied to synthetic content that creates a false impression of a product or service.
whyItMatters: If you buy, place, or just watch ads, a Pennsylvania airing can put a label on a spot that also runs elsewhere. The law is narrow enough that a shop flyer and a national commercial can both fall under it, and vague enough that two lawyers can disagree on the same image. The practical change is the label, not a ban on using the tool.
